will_get_coverage: likely across personal finance, mortgage, and business press in the run-up to the June 16-17 FOMC meeting

The 'most dissents since 1992' detail adds historical novelty that reporters will use.

The story is building toward a peak — pre-FOMC coverage is in the rising-to-peak stage, with rate-expectation pieces actively being written. The window for pre-decision expert commentary is open now and will remain open through the meeting

standing.rationale: A consumer-lending/mortgage fintech with first-party data on application volume and refinance demand tied to rate expectations, plus a named chief economist, has direct operational standing. Their data is the micro-level proof of what the macro rate story means for actual borrowers — exactly what personal finance and mortgage reporters want

window.rationale: The June 16-17 FOMC meeting is the live catalyst. Pre-decision pieces are being written now. The window is open for the run-up (now through June 15) and will reopen briefly post-decision for reaction commentary. This is the right time to pitch.

evidence_used.title: Fed holds at 3.5-3.75% through three meetings; 8-4 dissent split (most since 1992); possible first cut at June 16-17 FOMC

Whether the client's application data shows a clear pre-June-16 pattern that can be shared as exclusive data
honest_assessment: This is a strong newsjacking window. The combination of a live major macro story, a concrete dated catalyst (June 16-17 FOMC), and a client with first-party lending application data and a named economist creates a genuine opportunity that most consumer-lending companies cannot match. Personal finance and mortgage reporters will be writing pre-decision pieces now; they need sources who can show what borrower behavior looks like in real-time, not just macro analysis. Ride with data-forward commentary in the run-up to the meeting.

next_move.rationale: Draft a chief-economist-attributed comment backed by specific application-volume data, positioned for personal finance and mortgage reporters in the pre-FOMC run-up window
